newsitem.title: USA: American Intl has higher results for quarter, year.
newsitem.headline: American Intl has higher results for quarter, year.

text.p: American International Group Inc., a major insurance, pension and financial services company, reported higher fourth-quarter and full-year earnings Thursday.

"All areas of life operations did very well in 1996," AIG Chairman M.R. Greenberg said. "The privatisation of government pension programmes in Latin America is accelerating and AIG is a leading player in this area," he added.

AIG had fourth-quarter earnings, before capital gains, of $759.9 million, or $1.61 a share. A year earlier, it earned $489.3 million, or $1.40 a share. Revenues rose to $7.42 billion from $6.86 billion a year earlier.

For the year, AIG earned $2.84 billion, or $6.03 a share, before capital gains, compared with $2.46 billion, or $5.20 a share, a year earlier. Revenues rose to $28.2 billion from $25.9 billion in 1995.
Premium income rose 13.6 percent in the fourth quarter after foreign exchange to $2.47 billion and rose 11.7 percent to $8.98 billion for the year.
Operating income rose 19.5 percent in the quarter and 21.8 percent for the full year to a 1996 total of $1.29 billion, AIG said.

Shortly after year-end, AIG announced its new joint venture pension management company in Mexico and said its growing overseas consumer finance businesses were augmented in 1996 with the purchase of Hong Kong-based SPC Credit Ltd.
It said its financial services business had a strong year, with operating income up 25.4 percent to $524 million.
AIG's stock was off 75 cents at $124.875 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
